title: Consolidate credential field interactions: strength meter, copy affordance, and validation anchoring
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Problem: Credential inputs (passwords, API keys, tokens) have a growing set of ad-hoc behaviors across products: inline strength meters that shift layout, copy-to-clipboard buttons positioned inconsistently, and validation messages that either appear under fields or only in a top-level summary. This creates visual jitter, token mismatch across density modes, and accessibility gaps for screen reader users. Goal: Define a single, token-driven pattern for credential inputs that covers layout (icons/affordances), motion-reduced strength feedback, clipboard affordance, and a clear rule for when to anchor validation inline vs. in a summarized list.
acceptance_criteria: A single design spec exists (Figma) showing credential input variants: default, compact, with strength meter, with copy affordance, and error/soft-error states
All visual spacing and color values are expressed in design tokens (padding, gap, icon spacing, strength bar colors) and map to runtime tokens used by the component library
Strength meter must not change height of form rows when updated; transitions must respect prefers-reduced-motion
Copy-to-clipboard control has a stable hit target, visible focus state, and an accessible name for screen readers

Validation anchoring behavior documented: inline for single-field validation; summary + focus-anchor for multi-field form submissions; keyboard focus moves to first invalid field when summary item clicked
Design spec includes keyboard and screen-reader interactions, and a QA checklist for accessibility tests
design_decisions: Use an inline strength bar that lives in an absolutely positioned overlay located within the field container so updates do not affect layout flow
Strength bar visual scale will be expressed as three tokenized buckets (weak | medium | strong) with both color and non-color cues (pattern + label) to satisfy contrast and color-blind scenarios
Copy affordance will be a trailing icon button within the input's affix area; on copy success it temporarily switches to a check icon and exposes an aria-live polite announcement
Inline validation appears immediately on blur for single-field interactions; for form-level submit validation we show a summary at the top and add anchor links that set focus to the target field
Compact density uses a smaller token set but preserves 44x44 touch-friendly hit targets for interactive affordances by expanding hit area with negative margins behind visual elements
tradeoffs: Absolute positioning for the strength bar prevents layout jitter but is more complex to implement with variable field heights — implementation must handle multiline and textarea targets
Providing non-color visual cues increases visual complexity in the spec (pattern overlays) but is necessary for accessibility compliance
Keeping consistent copy affordance across compact and default densities requires invisible hit-area engineering; small visual buttons may look less native but improve accessibility
deliverables: Finalized Figma file with tokenized layers and component variants
Design tokens mapping document (token name -> role) in Confluence
Example markup and CSS/Token snippets for engineers (HTML/CSS + React props contract)
Accessibility QA checklist and automated test hints for E2E tests
A short demo story in the component library showing credential input behaviors with knobs
implementation_notes: Runtime must provide three token groups: input.affix.gap, input.affix.hitArea, credential.strength.{weak,medium,strong}.{color,pattern,ariaLabel}
Strength meter should publish its score to aria-valuenow on an element with role=progressbar; announce changes only on blur unless explicit user request for live updates
Copy action should call navigator.clipboard.writeText and on success toggle an ephemeral state for 1.6s; ensure failures surface a non-modal inline error
Provide a single boolean prop 'validationSummaryMode' to toggle between inline-first vs. summary-first flows for product teams
Edge cases: password managers and browser autofill must not overlay the strength bar; include z-index guidance and a test matrix for common managers
qa_checks: Keyboard-only: Tab to input, operate reveal/copy affordances with Enter/Space; focus order preserved
Screen reader: NVDA/VoiceOver reads input label, hint, and shows strength via progressbar with aria-label
Motion reduced: With 'prefers-reduced-motion' set, strength transitions are instant
Contrast: Strength bar patterns pass 3:1 for small UI; color-only not relied upon
Form submit: Trigger validation summary and click anchor -> focus lands on field and screen reader announces message
